excerpt: Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar. Vanishment contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina's clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.

In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peters Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs.

A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene's outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There's a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.

Live at Rockpalast 1999 documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm Mac Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Taped at the height of Dr. John's international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.

artist: Mats Edén, Tellef Kvifte, Knut Kvifte Nesheim
excerpt: Króta features Swedish fiddler Mats Edén and Norwegians Tellef Kvifte on flutes, and drummer Knut Kvifte Nesheim. The trio offers a far from conventional take on the traditional tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music.

True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Sendas is described as the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. Unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in an empty concert hall.

Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary.

After nine previous albums and a 25-year career at the forefront of world music, Lucas Santtana is fluent in the many genres of Brazilian music. His new project, Brasiliano, is a musical exploration of the languages of Brazil.

This expanded 15th anniversary edition marks a good time to look back at the band's mix of Piedmont string band and traditional music, nestling beside early 20th century blues, and a few original and modern pieces in the mix.

album: A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking
excerpt: A double CD album from two Malian musicians whose project began in 2013 when Neba Solo (balafon) and Benego Diakité (n'goni) were recorded by Bamako producer Ousmane Haïdara.
Vida (Spanish for Life) is the third release by Catalan guitarist/composer Dani Jané. The album is described as a lyrical, rhythmically driven work that synthesizes diverse musical traditions.

Il Mito (The Myth) is a celebration album marking 50 years of Canzoniere Grecanico Salentino (CGS) - a band that pioneered the charged, hypnotic pizzica sound and helped break it from its southern Italian homeland onto the world stage.
Fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku after a lengthy break. The album explores the intersection of Finnish folk music with Niku's deep love of Balkan music.

A collaboration between the five-piece Belgian instrumental group WÖR and Kongero, the acclaimed Swedish female acapella folk quartet. Despite appearing to be an unlikely musical pairing, they prove to be pretty much musical best friends.

Stelios Petrakis is recognized as one of the foremost players of the Cretan lyra. True to its title, the album focuses on Petrakis's lyra and laouto, featuring a panoply of other traditional instruments played by musicians of equal stature.

Polish artist Maria Ka discovered her family's Jewish roots, leading to immersion in Jewish studies and the Yiddish language. Di Mashin features original songs in Yiddish embracing politically active feminism and committed meta-universality.

Echo is Emi Makabe's second recording on Sunnyside Records, a generous meditation on resilience and legacy focused on the passing of her father. The title reflects the connections between generations.

Haitian-Canadian musician-composer born in Montreal who plays an impressive variety of instruments. Over the course of 2025, Omicil released sMiLes one song per month, each accompanied by a philosophizing podcast.

An album built on compromises? No. The Visit isn't an easy listen, but it is eminently satisfying. The Visit pushes and cajoles Derksen's visions with raw, unfettered beauty, made with passion and no restraints.

Sound Bites: Short reviews featuring The Kasambwe Brothers and Madalitso Band (Malawi), Mahotella Queens (South Africa), Ebo Taylor (Ghana), Pelengana Blo (Mali), Five Day Miracle Tent Crusade, Novalima (Peru), Marco Bosco (Brazil), Monsieur Doumani (Cyprus), Martha Mavroidi (Greece/Cyprus), Kapela Rej (Belarus), Daj Ognia (Poland), Karolina Wegrzyn (Poland), The New Eves (UK), Orchestre Tout Puissant Marcel Duchamp (Belgium), Peixe e Limão (Italy/Belgium), and more.
